The tsymbaly is the Ukrainian version of the hammer dulcimer, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 314.122-4,5. It is a trapezoid box with steel or bronze metal strings, mostly in courses of three to five tuned in unison, with wound strings for some of the bass. The player strikes the strings with two short beaters, traditionally with leather-covered heads. It is common in the Ukrainian folk trio ensemble (Troyista muzyka), together with the violin, basolia, sopilka or bubon; in Ukrainian orchestras and conservatory courses the concert instrument has replaced most of the small folk instruments.
奇姆巴利琴為烏克蘭弦鳴樂器，以兩支短槌擊弦發聲，傳統槌頭以皮革包裹。胡楚爾型以頸: The tsymbaly is a Ukrainian chordophone sounded by striking the strings with two short beaters, traditionally with leather-covered heads. The Hutsul type hangs from a neck strap with the edge against the waist; the concert type stands on a four-legged frame and has a damper pedal. The strings are in courses of 3 to 5 in unison, and the bass may be one or two wound strings in unison. A beginner can start with holding the beaters, striking the strings, recognising the unison courses and tuning.
小型多弦弦鳴樂器最早見於公元前3500年亞述壁畫，被認為源自波斯桑圖爾琴，中世紀: The earliest small multi-string chordophones appear in Assyrian reliefs of 3500 BC, and the instrument is thought to come from the Persian santur, reaching Europe in the Middle Ages. After the rise of Viennese piano making in the nineteenth century, metal tuning pins and steel strings became easier to get, and the struck zither became popular in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, carried by Jewish and Roma travelling musicians to Ukraine and elsewhere, where local folk and concert versions took shape. The tsymbaly is first documented in the seventeenth century; the twentieth century brought the small Hutsul instrument and the semi-concert instruments made at the Chernihiv factory from 1950 to 1986, and in the 1870s the Hungarian Schunda concert instrument later replaced the smaller folk instruments in Ukrainian orchestras.

The source states that its trapezoid body is strung with metal strings, of steel or bronze, and that the bass may have one or two wound strings. The beaters are traditionally leather-covered, and there are also metal tuning pins, piano wire and metal tuning pegs. The materials of the body wood, the pedal, the strap and the other parts are not stated.
齊姆巴利琴音色明亮清脆，具有獨特的金屬質感。由於採用鋼或青銅弦被槌棒敲擊，產生的: The tsymbaly has a bright, clear timbre with a distinctive metallic quality. Because steel or bronze strings are struck with beaters, the sound is warm without losing its edge, full and penetrating. The instrument covers a wide range, from a deep bass to a brilliant treble. The courses of several strings tuned together make the sound fuller, and the resonance is strong and immediate. Beside the depth of a piano the tsymbaly is more agile and light; beside the guzheng its sound has more metallic sheen and less of the guzheng's warm elegance. This quality gives it a particular place in Ukrainian national music, able to play a soft melody and to show ardour as well.
